title: UK ETS 2026-2030 ultra-small-emitter monitoring and exit QA controls

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: UK ETS: Guidance for ultra small emitters
UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS): technical guidance and tools

facts.source_fact: An installation is a USE for 2026-2030 only if it is included on the official 2026-2030 USE list.
Eligibility pathways use reportable-emissions limits of 2,499 tCO2e or below for specified historic scheme years, depending on activity start date.
A USE must continue to monitor its emissions.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat opt-out status as no-monitoring status.

facts.source_fact: USE emissions monitoring follows the methodology in the installation monitoring plan, which must remain up to date and fit for purpose.
facts.expected_handling: Bind emissions to the approved methodology.

facts.source_fact: A USE must notify its regulator if emissions exceed 2,500 tCO2e in a scheme year.
An installation cannot voluntarily cease to be a USE during an allocation period.
facts.expected_handling: Do not invent an elective mid-period exit.

facts.source_fact: For the 2026-2030 allocation period, USE status is lost if reportable emissions exceed 2,500 tCO2e in any of scheme years 2026, 2027 or 2028.
If USE status ceases, the installation must notify the regulator by 31 March of that scheme year or risk a civil penalty.
After USE status ends, the regulator requires return to the main UK ETS scheme or application for HSE status if eligible.
facts.expected_handling: Route to the correct permit pathway.

facts.source_fact: Unpaid penalties and sanctions arising during USE status remain liable after USE status ends.
facts.expected_handling: Do not clear historic liabilities on status conversion.

guard_patterns.handling: Use the correct eligibility years for start date.
Keep 2,499 eligibility and >2,500 exit/notice logic explicit.
Route ended USE status to main scheme or eligible HSE pathway.
Use current-linked guidance and 2026-2030 allocation context.
Do not infer parcel emissions from USE status.
Flag list, threshold, year or permit conflicts.
